claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr in the untreated, as-cast state.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance.
Pack cementation can introduce aluminum into the near-surface region of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Embedding the alloy in an aluminum-rich powder mixture at around 1000 °C for a short duration facilitates aluminum diffusion into its near-surface region.
Surface aluminizing will produce a continuous, thin, and adherent Al2O3 scale on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature air exposure.
Near-surface aluminum enrichment promotes formation of a slow-growing protective alumina scale.
Alumina has sufficiently low oxygen permeability to act as a barrier to oxygen transport.
The alumina barrier will reduce oxidation and pesting of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The surface treatment can reduce oxidation without altering the alloy's bulk microstructure or mechanical properties.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit significantly lower oxygen uptake than untreated material.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain better surface integrity than untreated material.
The aluminized alloy will retain useful room-temperature ductility and high-temperature strength at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed oxidation-protection boundary is approximately 800 °C in air for a 5-hour exposure.
